avoid_for: Dark-mode-first products, luxury/minimal premium brands where yellow would read as noise, dense data UIs, and any context needing shadow-based depth, multiple accent colors, or more than two font weights.
best_for: Large consumer retail and e-commerce editorial homepages, product-heavy brand storytelling built around one strong brand color, and flat Scandinavian identities — media-led card grids with a single yellow action plane doing all the interface work.
name: IKEA
palette_voice: Pure white (#ffffff) and Warm White (#fffefb) surfaces with Ink Black (#111111) for text and dominant borders; IKEA Yellow (#ffdb00) is the singular chromatic workhorse — solid fills for CTAs and featured cards, never a border, never a text color, never decoration; Link Blue (#0159a3) is reserved strictly for text links; zero shadows and zero gradients — depth comes from yellow-vs-white contrast, image overlays, and spacing.
signature_moves: The Yellow CTA Card — a solid #ffdb00 plane + bold black headline + circular black arrow button, the unmistakable primary-action signature
Exactly one border radius in the whole system: 8px on cards, images, inputs, buttons, everything — flat-pack modular uniformity
A binary 400/700 weight system — hierarchy is forced through size and color alone, never extra weights
Gradient-to-black overlays at 30–60% opacity on every image card that carries text
The circular black arrow button (~40px, white arrow) as the universal 'navigate' affordance
typographic_voice: A sole custom sans (Noto IKEA, subst. Inter/DM Sans) at exactly two weights — 700 for headlines (36–51px, tight negative tracking down to -0.029em, compressed architectural quality) and 400 for body (16px, generous 1.57 line-height); no italics, no medium, no light weights; the negative tracking is structural, not decorative.
